thread.title: Sixth Day of Gains for Dow Has Bears Confused

title: Sixth Day of Gains for Dow Has Bears Confused
text:
Sixth Day of Gains for Dow Has Bears Confused By aapl
Another solid day for the indices has many market players questioning their recent bearishness. The DJIA is now up six days in a row, the S&P 500 has busted above a key downtrend line and the gain in the Nasdaq 100 off of recent lows is approaching 5%.
A week ago the market was struggling and the narrative was that if stocks can't rally on very good earnings, then what will it take to move the market higher? Apparently, the answer to that question is Warren Buffett. Since the disclosure that he added to his Apple ( AAPL ) position, stocks have been on a rampage.
Sentiment shifted so quickly following the Buffett news that we have seen a return to the pattern of big-picture negatives no longer having any impact. Trump's pullout from the Iran nuclear deal was an ideal "sell the news" setup with the indices facing resistance but turned into a bear trap instead.
The momentum continued today with a soft CPI report that rallied bonds and caused the dollar to pull back. Rather than looking for technical resistance to be a problem, market players are now worried that they have insufficient long exposure.
The bullish spin on this action is that it is a delayed reaction to good earnings and is being helped by decreased concern about inflation. The bearish spin on this action is primarily confusion. There is a long list of macro concerns, negative seasonality and a deteriorating technical picture -- until the last few days.
Is the bull market action back? Many buyers seemed to think so today. But we have had several energetic rallies since the top in January and they have all ended badly.
